Jade (ACME): Hey team — seeing repeated SSE disconnects and partial payloads. Stream closes mid-chunk, client reconnects, then we get duplicate billing for the same conversation. Request id r=abc123 at 2026-03-16T22:12:14Z. Help? :grimacing:
Sam (support): Sorry about that. Can you paste a minimal repro curl and a short log excerpt? Also which client (mobile/web/proxy) and region?
Jade (ACME): Using our mobile SDK (iOS), region eu-west-1. Minimal repro curl I ran locally:
```bash
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***" \ 
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \ 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=xl-8k"
```
Logs around disconnect (client timestamp):
```
[22:12:13] connection established r=abc123
[22:12:14] sent chunk id=1 len=512
[22:12:14] partial chunk delivered id=1 status=200
[22:12:14] socket write failed: EPIPE
[22:12:14] closing connection r=abc123 reason=slowconsumer
```
Sam (support): Thanks. Two quick asks: 1) can you enable a short tcpdump on client side when repro'ing? 2) Can you reproduce via curl from a laptop on same network? Helps rule out mobile SDK buffering.
Jade (ACME): Yep can do, repros from laptop too. Attaching short pcap in the ticket. Also noticed spikes in billed token counts — looks like reconnect attempts counted as new streams.
Devon (eng-runtime): Interesting — logs show server did a hard close after write errors. Possibilities: upstream proxy (customer side or infra) hit sndbuf and returned EAGAIN/EPIPE, or our side tried a standby handoff to another worker but the socket was half-closed.
Devon (eng-runtime): Can you share the exact server-side request id from your pcap TLS connection? Also which SDK version — older SDKs did aggressive reconnect with no resume token, leading to duplicate billing.
Jade (ACME): SDK v0.9.1 — we haven't updated to the new resume behavior. Server request id in TLS SNI: r=abc123.
Maria (oncall): I'm putting this onpager. Devon, can you check if the front-proxy shows repeated RSTs or proxy buffer saturation for r=abc123?
Devon (eng-runtime): Looking at edge logs for r=abc123:
```
edge-1 | 22:12:13 accept conn id=42 from 10.10.10.5
edge-1 | 22:12:13 proxy -> runtime stream r=abc123 queued
edge-2 | 22:12:14 proxy write -> client returned EAGAIN after 64KB
runtime-3 | 22:12:14 runtime observed send error EPIPE on fd 182
runtime-3 | 22:12:14 attempted standby handoff to runtime-5 but peer not writable
runtime-3 | 22:12:14 aborting connection r=abc123 reason=slowconsumer.write-fail
```
Devon (eng-runtime): That "standby handoff" line is the interesting bit — the runtime attempted to move the active stream to another worker (for draining / maintenance), but the downstream socket buffer was full and the handoff couldn't complete. Our current behavior is to abort when handoff fails to avoid head-of-line blocking.
Sam (support): Is that abort policy expected? Means customers with slow clients get immediate connection resets during maintenance?
Devon (eng-runtime): It's a tradeoff. We do immediate abort to keep tail latency predictable. But we can improve: 1) softer backoff (keep trying short window) 2) advertise smaller chunks / more frequent flushes to reduce sndbuf pressure 3) SDK resume token (so reconnects don't double-bill).
Jade (ACME): What can we do now? Customers are hitting this in production.
Devon (eng-runtime): Short-term mitigations for you: - upgrade SDK to v1.2+ (adds resume token and jittered reconnect) - set header X-Redwood-Stream-Chunk-Size: 256 to force smaller writes - ensure your mobile proxy isn't adding large buffering (some proxies coalesce small writes)
Devon (eng-runtime): Longer-term, we'll open an internal ticket to change abort policy to try a 500ms buffered handoff window before abort and to surface a metric when handoff fails.
Maria (oncall): Filed INC-2026-467. I'm adding telemetry: handoff_fail_count, per-edge sndbuf_fill_ratio, and runtime_send_error_rate. Also enabling a short-term override: do not abort on handoff failure for non-critical tiers (customer trial).
OpsBot: alert: INC-2026-467 created by Maria (oncall) — assigned to eng-runtime.
Sam (support): Thanks. Jade, we'll monitor INC and follow up when eng ships the override and the SDK patch. Meanwhile please try SDK v1.2 and the smaller-chunk header — LMK results.
Jade (ACME): Will try SDK v1.2 + chunk header and report back. Appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:
